title: Brane-tower argument for the critical exponent's dependence on $\chi(A)$ alone
html:
Remark. Brane-tower argument for the critical exponent's dependence on \chi(A) alone

Argument from the brane tower. Euler characteristic stability states that \chi(E_n) = \chi(A) across the brane tower. The critical exponent \alpha is determined by two quantities that depend only on this uniform structure:

  1. The Sobolev constant scaling. The Sobolev constant C_q depends on the eigenvalue growth rate [k]_q^2. This is determined by the representation theory of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) — a categorical invariant.
  2. The cascade depth scaling. The number of active modes depends on \mathrm{Re}_q, which is a function of q alone. The Kolmogorov scaling \Omega \sim N^{5/3} follows from d = 3 and quadratic nonlinearity.

The initial energy E_0 affects the prefactor of the enstrophy evolution bound, but not the exponent. The critical exponent \alpha = 4/3 derives from the cascade depth scaling.

Universality class. Different QOU realisations (different \chi(A)) could in principle give different \alpha, because \chi(A) affects the embeddable torus knot species, modifying the nonlinear interaction count.
